text:
alyssa: FYI rolling alert after last night's driver rollout in us-west2. A small but growing number of H100 jobs are failing at ptx compilation time. Saw first in a canary, now ~18 hosts.

alyssa: sample error in pods:```
ptxas info :  CUDA Ptxas 12.2, info 
ptxas fatal : Unsupported GPU architecture 'sm_90' in ptx file
Error: ptxas returned non-zero exit code 255
```

devon: which driver version rolled? is this the 536.x push?

alyssa: 536.14 pushed at 02:10 UTC. Canary passed for most models, but hopper workloads that rely on JIT-ing ptx at runtime are erroring.

infra-bot: [ALERT] 18 hosts reporting ptxas failures - group: h100-us-west2-pool - incident id INC-20260318-ptx-01 : https://incidents/company/INC-20260318-ptx-01

sam: this reads like a mismatch between the driver CUDA toolkit expectations and the sm90-compiled PTX emitted by our kernels. Two quick options: pin the fleet back to previous driver, or force nodes to use cached/cubin kernels (if available) to avoid JIT.

olivia: confirmed NCCL logs also show some P2P initialization timeouts on the same hosts, probably fallout from the failed kernel loads. We're seeing job restarts and autoscaler draining a few nodes which is spiking cost.

matt: can we isolate to a subset of images? are these containers building their own PTX (nvcc) at runtime or bundling PTX blobs?

alyssa: most affected workloads are our internal throughput tests and a few customer canaries that still rely on on-instance `ptxas` JIT for model kernels. The model packaging team bundles PTX for sm_86 and emits sm_90 for optimized paths in a postbuild step — so some flows assume the driver/toolkit can JIT sm_90.

devon: immediate mitigation: 1) add a temporary capacity switch to route new Hopper traffic to h100-eu and h100-east pools (no driver roll yet there), 2) mark us-west2 h100 pool as maintenance so autoscaler avoids placing new tasks. That will reduce cost churn.

sam: agree. Also preparing a rollback of 536.14 to 535.86 as a safety fallback. Need a config freeze window of 20m.

alyssa: I'm going to run a quick grep across images for embedded `sm_90` PTX blobs and list the customer canaries that still JIT.

olivia: action item for runtime team: add a runtime flag to prefer cubin cache and skip ptx JIT when environment variable REDWOOD_FORCE_CUBIN=1 is set. Can we get that shipped as a hotfix?

matt: we can push a lightweight release that checks for the env and preloads cubin. If binaries already lack cubin we need a longer fix: recompile kernels at build time targeting sm_90 or include cubins in the image. That will take a bit.

infra-bot: [TASK] Created ticket INFRA-PTX-2026 to track rollback, routing changes, and hotfix. Assigned to devon and matt.

devon: rolling rollback scheduled in 15m for canaries only. Will update slack with results.

alyssa: if rollback doesn't clear P2P timeouts we may need to force a full node reboot to clear driver state. That will be disruptive; deferring to ops for approval.

sam: for postmortem: we'll add a preflight that validates `ptxas` and a small sm_90 JIT smoke test against an H100 in each region before rolling drivers. Also add a gating check for NCCL P2P bring-up.

olivia: noting cost impact: autoscaler drained ~5 nodes and re-provisioned replacement instances in other regions — estimate ~$2.1k over 12 hours if not contained. tagging finance.

matt: update from rollback canary: 3 of 3 canary jobs succeeded after rolling back to 535.86. Pushing rollback to remaining us-west2 h100 nodes now (staggered).

alyssa: thanks. keep monitoring for any remaining sm90-related errors. If we see other regions impacted, follow same routing/maintenance pattern.

devon: after stabilization we'll prepare a coordinated upgrade plan: ensure model packaging includes cubin or ensure driver/toolkit combo supports PTX target. Also update docs for "driver min" per model variant.

sam: I'll own the postmortem and the automation for the preflight suite.

alyssa: good. tagging @oncall for visibility. :eyes:
